title: Reference exemplar cohort evaluation and drift inspector for embedding/rerank endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a reproducible offline evaluation and monitoring system that validates embedding + reranker accuracy across temporal cohorts, supports per-model/per-version comparisons, and generates deterministic alerts when quality or distributional characteristics drift. This ticket delivers: (1) a curated set of reference exemplars ("exemplar cohorts") with provenance and versioning; (2) an offline scoring pipeline that computes recall@k, MRR, ranking-stability, calibration and embedding-distribution metrics for scheduled runs; (3) statistical drift inspector that compares current traffic cohorts against reference cohorts and emits graded signals (warning/critical) using multiple tests (KS on similarity distributions, centroid shift, embedding norm drift, and recall delta); and (4) ops integration (dashboards, incident runbooks, and PagerDuty hooks) and a lightweight labelling workflow to refresh exemplars.
acceptance_criteria: Exemplar cohort metadata stored in S3 with stable schema and semantic tags (domain, time-window, label-source, model-version)
Nightly offline scorer that runs across models: outputs: recall@1/5/10, MRR, ranking stability (top-k overlap) and calibration curve CSVs
Drift inspector running daily: produces KS p-values, centroid L2 distance, and a combined drift score; thresholds configurable per-project
Alerts: warning when recall@5 drops by >6% vs reference; critical if combined drift score exceeds configured threshold and recall regression >10%
Dashboards: per-model historical trend for metrics + distribution viz (similarity histograms, centroid trajectory)
Label workflow: Slack-to-labeler link to surface candidate exemplars for curator review and automatic replacement process with audit trail
activity_log: 2026-02-15 - Ticket created by Aisha Patel: initial problem statement and outline of deliverables; linked to product request PRD.
2026-02-18 - Design sync with PM (Nora Kim) and LA on acceptable detection thresholds; agreed on dual-signal approach (distributional + quality metric).
2026-02-22 - Implementation plan reviewed: use batch Spark job for nightly scoring and a lightweight Go service for drift scoring; chosen KS + centroid methods for initial rollout.
2026-02-26 - Prototype run: offline scorer produced recall@5 MRR CSVs for 3 models; observed a 4% variance between dataset slices; logged artifacts.
2026-03-01 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4822 implements scoring pipeline and S3 schema. Code review requested from eng-data and infra owners.
2026-03-03 - Load test: nightly scorer finishes in ~14 minutes for baseline 50k exemplar set; bottleneck identified in nearest-neighbor computation; task created to add faiss sharding (ENG-714161).
notes: Implementation choices: use Faiss for nearest-neighbor speedup, store exemplar vectors with deterministic IDs and provenance metadata; scoring pipeline supports pluggable metrics. Trade-offs: initial rollout will sample a compact exemplar cohort (50k) to keep nightly runtime under 20m; later expand with sharding and incremental scoring. Next: add synthetic perturbation probes and label noise estimation.
